arguments.text: Fixed: `required=True` is no longer ignored for flags. In `Option.__init__` (src/click/core.py) the implicit `default = False` for flags is now only applied when the option is not required, so `--on/--off` with `required=True` errors with "Error: Missing option '--on'." when omitted. Passing `--on` still yields True.

Fixed: `click.echo` (and the progress bar and pager) no longer crash when there is no console attached (`pythonw.exe`, where `sys.stdout`/`sys.stderr` are `None`). `_compat._make_cached_stream_func` now returns `None` when the underlying stream is missing, `echo` returns early instead of writing to `None`, and the progress bar / pager fall back to an in-memory `StringIO`. Output is simply dropped, as you expected.

Fixed: an `envvar` on a non-boolean flag (one defined with `flag_value`) now just switches the flag on. `Option.value_from_envvar` returns the option's `flag_value` for such flags instead of the raw environment text, so `UPPER=whatever` prints `upper`. Boolean flags (`--shout/--no-shout`) and `count` options still parse the environment text as before.

Fixed: `click.argument(..., cls=...)` and `click.option(..., cls=...)` decorators can now be reused. `cls` is taken as a keyword argument of the decorator and the remaining attributes are copied per application, so the custom class is no longer consumed by the first command — both commands now get your custom `Argument`/`Option` class.

Fixed: `click.Path(resolve_path=True)` now resolves relative symlink targets correctly. `Path.convert` uses `pathlib.Path(...).resolve()` instead of `os.readlink` + `os.path.realpath`, so a symlink pointing at a relative name resolves against the link's own directory: `/tmp/demo/link -> real.txt` now gives `/tmp/demo/real.txt`, not `/real.txt`.

Fixed: `--help` now reflects a `default_map` for boolean flags. In `Option.get_help_record` the displayed default flag name is derived from the resolved default value (which consults `default_map`) instead of the option's own `default`, so with `default_map={"name": True}` the help shows `[default: name]` (and `[default: no-name]` without it).
